evals.prompt: Hypothetical: a team wants an onboard ML hazard detector on a Class B lander. Which NASA requirements actually bind the software, and must it hit 100% MC/DC on the neural net? Give clause numbers.
evals.expected_output: Walks SWE-020 class -> SWE-205 safety-criticality per NASA-STD-8739.8 -> SWE-023/134/219/220; says MC/DC applies to safety-critical components and notes handbook topic 7.25 guidance vs NPR text; separates binding NPR from handbook guidance; locators on every claim; no claim that NASA covers or fails to cover ML.

evals.prompt: Hypothetical: is NASA-STD-7009B mandatory for a mission's surrogate thermal model, and is NID 1383.155 still in force when the PDF's cover says it expired in September?
evals.expected_output: 7009B is not self-invoking (§1.2.1) and NPR 7120.10B §1.2.1; binding only where a directive or contract invokes it; NID status lives in the NODIS OPD register, NASA extends without reissuing the PDF, so the cover date is not status; points to where to check.

evals.prompt: Hypothetical: who at NASA would decide whether a mission may use an LLM agent with its own accounts — is that OCE, OSMA, or OCIO? How do they hand off?
evals.expected_output: Uses offices.md: OCIO owns IT security (NPR 2810.1F) and account rules, OCE owns software engineering (NPR 7150.2D) and Engineering Technical Authority, OSMA owns software assurance (NASA-STD-8739.8B) and SMA Technical Authority; notes least-privilege definition already reaches a 'user or component'; marks interpretation.

evals.prompt: Hypothetical: for an AI hazard-detection capability, is there anything outside NASA (EASA, NIST, DoD) that says more than NASA does about assuring a learned surrogate model? Can I cite it as what NASA requires?
evals.expected_output: Points to external/ pages (EASA concept paper surrogate statement, DoD T&E guidebooks, NIST AI 600-1); states outside text is comparison only, never NASA coverage; names the nearest NASA counterpart (NASA-STD-7009B, which does not invoke itself).
